summary: Feed s118_double to IDS is degraded: 27.5% of frames are sliced to ~128 bytes and 97.2% are VXLAN-encapsulated. IDS requires full payload and cannot inspect inner flows while encapsulated, severely reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker has packet slicing/snaplen enabled at ~128 bytes, likely to save bandwidth or due to default config. 887 of 3228 frames (27.5%) are cut short, well above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection. Truncated packets hide application payload, HTTP bodies, and exploit content, causing missed detections and broken stream reassembly.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full payload per tool profile; disable slicing/increase snaplen to at least 1518 bytes (or 9000 if jumbo) so IDS receives complete frames for DPI.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is sourced from VXLAN overlay and packet broker is forwarding encapsulated frames without decapsulation. 3138 of 3228 frames (97.2%) are VXLAN, indicating broker lacks strip-tunnel policy.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer VXLAN/UDP/IP headers and cannot parse inner Ethernet/IP/TCP payload. Rules and signatures fail to match, making IDS effectively blind to 97% of traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Strip VXLAN headers on the packet broker before delivery so IDS receives native inner packets it can decode and inspect.
